extracted.intended_audience: microbiologists, bacterial taxonomists, members of nomenclature committees and code drafters
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements for preparing, amending, and applying the International Code of Nomenclature of Bacteria (including Approved Lists, Validation Lists, types and orthography). Intended for those who create or apply bacteriological taxonomic names and the Code's provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of names in a limited range of publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Publication of names in a limited range of publications (provision proposed to be embodied in the Revised Code).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drafting Committee proposed restricting valid publication of new names to a defined set of recognized outlets to improve reliability and traceability of nomenclatural acts; this was an objective in the complete revision (1968–1970).

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligate designation of types
rubrics_metrics.description: Obligate designation of types for new taxa (mandatory when publishing names).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Revised Code was to embody obligate designation of nomenclatural types as a requirement for valid publication, to stabilise application of names.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods for designation and preservation of type strains
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods on designation and the preservation of type strains must be specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Drafting Committee included requirements for how types (especially type strains) are to be designated and preserved, reflecting concerns about accessibility and long-term availability of culture types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimal descriptions of taxa
rubrics_metrics.description: Minimal descriptions of taxa should be required for valid publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Revised Code aimed to require minimal diagnostic information so that taxa are meaningfully defined at publication rather than relying on later, separate descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alteration to provisions for amending the Code
rubrics_metrics.description: Change the procedural provisions governing how the Code itself is amended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revision of the Code included alterations to amendment procedures to reflect organizational changes in the International Committee and to make the Code's amendment process workable in future.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annotation and explanation of revisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendations and revised Rules should be adequately annotated and note resemblances and differences to Botanical and Zoological Codes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial Board recommended that emendations be published with annotations and comparisons to other codes and that significant resemblances/differences be explicitly noted to aid users.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simultaneous publication/translation in major scientific languages
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim to publish the Code and significant translations (e.g., Spanish, German, French, Japanese) so that texts in other important languages are available alongside the English text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the manuscript preparation was time-consuming and translations were not always included, the hope was expressed that future printings would include simultaneous translations to increase accessibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance or removal of complex intra-genus categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Reduce or remove provisions controlling names of categories used almost only within one genus (Section, Subsection, Series, Subseries).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission felt it was retrograde to maintain complex rules for categories used mainly in Streptomyces and removed those provisions from the present Code to simplify nomenclature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approved Lists as a new starting point; excluded names lose standing
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare an Approved List containing all names with current usage and establish that names not included will lose standing in nomenclature from a future starting date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A radical proposal accepted: construct Approved Lists to serve as the basis for future nomenclature, so that names not on the Approved List would no longer have standing, while still allowing reuse of old names subject to homonym checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanism for conservation or blocking of well-established names
rubrics_metrics.description: Conserve or block publication of certain well-established names of international repute to maintain stability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discussion included conserving well-established names by blocking certain publications; disadvantages (need for detailed taxonomic work and many appeals) were noted, so conservation was considered carefully versus an Approved List approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisions for reviving names and limitations on revival
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for reviving names (including revival in new combinations) and clarifying the circumstances under which revival is justified (e.g., Rule 33d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisions for reviving names were clarified (Rule 33d); for sensitive groups (e.g., plant pathogens), recommendations exist that names be revived only for the original bacteria and with sound justification to avoid confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulation of infrasubspecific names requires cross-disciplinary consultation
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals to regulate nomenclature of infrasubspecific forms (previously subject only to good-practice recommendations) require consultation with epidemiologists, geneticists, biochemists and others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complexities around infrasubspecific taxa led to referral for further study and interdisciplinary consultation before adopting regulatory provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation mechanism for names effectively published outside IJSB (Rules 16, 27, 28)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarify application of Rules dealing with validation of names effectively published outside the International Journal (IJSB) and use of Validation Lists to validate such names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At later meetings the application of Rules 16 and 27 was clarified; names effectively published outside the IJSB can be validated through the IJSB Validation Lists (Rules 27 and 28) with clear procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule permitting rejection of perilous names (Rule 56)
rubrics_metrics.description: Permit rejection of a name whose application is likely to lead to dangers to health or serious economic consequences ('a perilous name').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A new provision added to Rule 56 allowed rejection of names likely to cause harm or serious economic problems, providing a safety valve to the Code for problematic epithets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nomenclatural types in Approved Lists are accepted unless changed by Commission
rubrics_metrics.description: Types listed in the Approved Lists are to be accepted as nomenclatural types unless formally changed by the Judicial Commission (Opinion 58).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opinion 58 confirmed the stability of types in Approved Lists, subject to change only by Commission action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation of subgenera (Rule 10c) and species-epithet conceptual flexibility (Rule 12a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarify citation conventions for subgenera (Rule 10c) and allow species epithets not necessarily to refer to a single, fixed concept (emendment to Rule 12a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 10c (subgenus citation) and Rule 12a (species-epithet concept) were amended to clarify citation practice and conceptual flexibility of epithets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority rules for names published in IJSB and its Validation Lists (Rule 24b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide provisions on priority of names published in the IJSB and in its Validation Lists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 24b contains provisions governing priority relationships when names appear in the journal and in Validation Lists, consolidating priority practices under the Code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orthography standards and Appendix 9 revision
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards on orthography, latinization conventions and taxonomic precedent (Appendix 9) should be specified and revised as needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendix 9 on Orthography was revised with expert advice to reconcile latinization conventions and taxonomic precedent; this includes guidance on formation and spelling of epithets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deposit of type strains in culture collections as a Rule (accessibility of types)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommend (and consider making a Rule) that type strains be deposited in culture collections; address accessibility issues such as strains under patent pending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There was discussion to elevate the recommendation that type strains be deposited to a mandatory Rule; concerns were raised that strains involved in patent applications were not readily available for deposit, highlighting the need to reconcile patent practice and deposit/accessibility requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply the Code to all prokaryotes (Bacteria and Archaea)
rubrics_metrics.description: Extend applicability of the Code to cover all prokaryotes, i.e., members of Bacteria and Archaea.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At Prague it was generally accepted that the Code should apply to both Bacteria and Archaea, broadening the Code's scope beyond classical bacteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisions for putative taxa (Candidatus)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration and provision for handling putative taxa designated 'Candidatus' that cannot meet standard type strain requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The issue of putative taxa (Candidatus) was raised, prompting work on recording properties of such taxa and on appropriate Code treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish minimal standards/principles for description of new taxa
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop principles for description of new taxa to assist subcommittees in drawing up minimal standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An editorial proposal recommended drafting principles for describing new taxa to provide consistent minimal descriptive standards across subcommittees and facilitate taxonomy work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexing and maintenance of lists of validly published names and nomenclatural changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain indices (e.g., Approved Lists, Indexes of nomenclatural changes, lists of names validly published in specified intervals) to document valid names and subsequent changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication and maintenance of Approved Lists (1 January 1980) and indexes of names/changes (e.g., 1980–1985, 1980–1989, 1980–1992) were used to provide a reliable record of valid names and track changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harmonization with other Codes where practicable (e.g., Cyanobacteria issue)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where organisms fall between codes (e.g., cyanobacteria/blue‑green algae), seek harmonization with Botanical Code officers and allow authors to choose nomenclatural code appropriate to their view.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposal to place Cyanobacteria under the Bacteriological Code led to long discussions about reconciling botanical and bacteriological practices; interim guidance allowed workers to name cyanobacteria under the Bacteriological Code if they considered them bacteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creation of separate Code/committee for viruses where necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize special nature of some organism groups (viruses) and establish separate rules/committee when Linnaean binary names are inappropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Virologists at the Moscow Congress prepared their own rules, leading to formation of a separate International Committee on Nomenclature of Viruses; shows criterion that groups with special needs may require separate codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish reference service laboratories and subcommittee restructuring
rubrics_metrics.description: Encourage establishment of reference service laboratories with excellence in particular methods and consider restructuring subcommittees to reflect technical needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prague discussions included setting up reference labs for method excellence and restructuring subcommittees, indicating organisational criteria to support nomenclatural standards and technical validation.
